introducoes.uso: FeatherSheet is a spreadsheet that runs entirely on your machine: no account, no login, none of your content leaves it. Here is how to use each part, from the basics (typing and writing formulas) to the advanced (pivot tables, FeatherQuery and macros). Follow along with the arrow, or pick a topic in the side menu.
introducoes.funcoes: Every function you can use in a formula, by category, with its arguments and what it does. Arguments in brackets are optional. Every function accepts its Portuguese or English name. Tip: pressing F1 while writing a formula opens right on the function under the cursor.
introducoes.macros: Macros are JavaScript and automate what you would do by hand: fill, format, switch sheets, create new functions for cells. Open them in Ferramentas → Macros. The spreadsheet is the sheet object; Ctrl+Enter runs and Ctrl+Z undoes the whole macro. Addresses use A1 notation ("B2", "A1:D10"); numeric rows and columns start at 1.
introducoes.atalhos: Keys that make the work faster. Fixed ones always apply; configurable ones can be changed in Settings → Shortcuts, and the key shown here is the one in effect now.

corpo: Click a cell and type. Enter confirms and moves down; Tab confirms and moves right; Esc cancels.
• F2 or double-click edits the cell without erasing it.

• When you type text that only one cell in the same column starts with ("Sup" → "Supermarket"), the full value shows below: Enter, Tab or clicking away accepts it; deleting a letter drops the suggestion.
• Ctrl + arrow jumps to the end of the data; with Shift, it selects up to there.
• Ctrl+Z undoes and Ctrl+Y redoes — whole macros included. Inserting or deleting rows and columns can be undone too.

Commands live in the ribbon at the top. Ctrl+F1 swaps the ribbon for drop-down menus and a compact toolbar (and back). In a narrow window, groups that do not fit become a button with the group name that opens the whole group; whatever still does not fit goes to More. Micro mode (View ▸ Window, or Settings): with the ribbon collapsed, the menus, the command search and the expand-ribbon button move up into the title bar, and the tab row disappears.
Every formula starts with "=". In this locale arguments are separated by "," and "." is the decimal point: =SUM(A1:A10, 0.5).
• A1 is a cell; A1:B10 is a range; $A$1 stays fixed when the formula is copied.
• Another sheet: 'My Sheet'!A1 (quotes are only needed when the name has a space).
• Functions accept their Portuguese or English name (SOMA or SUM). The full list is under "Spreadsheet functions".
While you type, suggestions and argument hints show up. Clicking or dragging on the grid inserts the reference; each colored reference box can be dragged (move) or pulled by its corner (resize).
Functions that return several cells (FILTER, UNIQUE, SORT, SEQUENCE…) spill the result down and to the right. If something is in the way, the cell shows #SPILL!.
Formula with an error: right-click the cell → "Explicar este erro" shows the failing part and how to fix it.

• Names (Formulas → Defined Names): Define Name, Manager, Create from Selection and Use in Formula. A name works in any formula: =SUM(Sales). Formulas → Calculation has Calculation Options and Calculate Now.

• Iterative calculation: a formula that depends on itself (A1 reads B1 and B1 reads A1) shows #CIRCULAR!. To have it repeat the calculation until it settles, turn on Settings › Sheet › Iterative calculation and choose the maximum number of iterations and the change at which it stops. Each F9 repeats the iterations.
• Drag the small square at the corner of the selection (the fill handle) to continue a series: 1, 2, 3…, dates, "Item 1, Item 2…" and formulas.
• Double-clicking the handle fills down to the end of the data in the neighbouring column.
• Months and weekdays continue their list (Jan, Feb, Mar…). For your own lists (S, M, L, XL), type them in Settings › Sheet › Custom fill lists.
• A single number is copied; hold Ctrl while dragging to count up (7, 8, 9). With a series, Ctrl does the opposite and copies.
• Ctrl+D copies the cell above downwards; Ctrl+R copies the cell on the left to the right.
• Dragging the border of the selection moves the cells; formulas that read the block follow along.
• Ctrl+Shift+V pastes values only.
• Home → Fill: Series… (linear, growth or date, with step and limit) and Flash Fill (Ctrl+E), which completes the column following the example you typed.
Sheets live in the bottom bar. "+" creates a new one (or Shift+F11); Ctrl+PageUp and Ctrl+PageDown switch sheets.
Right-click a sheet tab: rename, duplicate, change color, hide and unhide.

Copy sheet to another file… adds a copy of the sheet at the end of an existing .fshz or .xlsx (if the name is taken, it becomes "Name (2)"); Copy sheet to a new file… creates a file with only that sheet. The open file does not change. Formulas that read other sheets now read the sheets with the same name in the destination. A .xlsx with a password, or with parts FeatherSheet does not convert, is not rewritten.

Font, color, borders, alignment and number format (currency, %, decimals) are on the Home tab. The format painter copies formatting from one cell to others; Ctrl+1 opens Format Cells. The arrow next to the currency button picks the cell currency (dollar, euro, Swiss franc, rupee and every other currency in circulation, 155 in all); in Format Cells, Currency lists them all with search by name, code or symbol. The Indian, Pakistani and Nepalese rupees and the taka group in lakh and crore (12,34,567), and a number typed that way (12,34,567 or 1.23.45.678) is read as a number; the decimal buttons also work on the chosen currency.
• Conditional formatting (Home → Conditional): colors cells by rule — greater than, contains text, duplicates, custom formula, color scale and data bar.
• Banded colors (Home → Styles) stripes the rows; Cell styles applies a ready-made style.
• Freeze (View → Freeze) keeps the first rows or columns in place while you scroll.
• Ctrl+T turns the data into a table: header, stripes, total row and a filter on each column. The table grows by itself when you type right below it.
• Ctrl+Shift+L turns the filter on or off. Sort is on the Home and Data tabs.

• Insert → PivotTable summarizes the data: drag fields to rows, columns and values (sum, count, average, distinct count, median, quartiles…). Recommended PivotTables suggests ready-made summaries from the selection. The source accepts A1:D100, another sheet (Data!A1:D100) or a table name. Calculated field (in the panel): a formula such as [Price] * Quantity; type the start of a name and the matching fields appear below it, one click completes it. Calculated item (same place): choose a Rows or Columns field, give a name and a formula over its other items (North - South); the formula applies at each intersection, and totals do not add it.
• Slicer (Insert → Filters): buttons that filter a table or pivot with one click.

• On the PivotTable tab: Subtotals picks none, at top (on the group row) or at bottom (a "Total" row after the items); Collapse level and Expand level close or open one level of groups per click. Filter pages creates one sheet per item of the field in Filters. Group selection joins the Rows items (or, in the header, Columns items) selected in the grid into one item (Group1) that sums them all; typing over the label renames the group and Ungroup undoes it. Data → Consolidate combines ranges from several sheets (by position or by labels) at the active cell. To have the same field in Filters and in Rows or Columns, drag it from the field list to the second area; dragging from one area to another only moves it.
• Home → Cells: Insert, Delete and Format (row height, column width, AutoFit, hide and unhide, protection).
• Right-clicking a header also hides and unhides. A hidden column or row shows as a thicker line between its neighbors.
• Merge is in the Alignment group; its arrow opens Merge & center and Merge across.
• Paste special (Ctrl+Alt+V or the arrow under Paste): values only, formats only, transpose and more.
• Go To (F5 or Ctrl+G): jumps to a cell or name, or selects by type — formulas, constants, blanks, errors, visible cells only.

• Right-click the selection → Copy as picture: the range goes to the clipboard as a picture, as the screen shows it (borders, colors, number formats). Ctrl+V pastes it as a picture here or in another program.
Formulas → Formula Auditing:
• Trace Precedents (what the cell reads) and Trace Dependents (what reads the cell) draw arrows; Remove Arrows clears them.
• Show formulas displays the formula text instead of the result.
• Evaluate Formula calculates the formula piece by piece, to find where the result goes wrong.
• Watch Window follows chosen cells, even on other sheets, while you work.
• Explain Error shows the part that failed and how to fix it.
Data → Forecast:
• Goal Seek… finds the value of a cell that brings a formula to the result you want.
• Scenarios stores named sets of values to switch between and compare.
• Data Table… calculates a formula for a list of values (one or two variables); Refresh table recalculates it.
A formula can read another spreadsheet: =[Sales.fshz]Data!A1 or =SUM([Sales.fshz]Data!A1:A10). The value is stored in the file, and also goes into .xlsx.
Data → Queries → Refresh links brings the new values; Edit links changes or removes the source. For safety, a file opened from disk only reads the other one after you refresh.

• Insert → Illustrations: Pictures, Shapes, Icons and SmartArt (14 diagram categories; each box is a shape with editable text) float over the grid (drag to move, corners resize). Text group: Text box and WordArt; Symbols group: Equation and Symbol. Page Layout ▸ Arrange brings forward, sends backward, aligns and rotates the selected object; the Selection Pane lists the sheet objects (click selects, the eye hides, the arrows change the order).
• Image in cell… puts the image inside the cell, so it follows rows and columns. In formulas: =IMAGE(address) and =IMAGE.BASE64(text).
• Insert → Checkbox puts checkboxes in the selected cells; the cell is TRUE or FALSE.
• Insert link (Links group) and Comment are also on the Insert tab.

Select the data and use Insert → Charts: Recommended, or a type directly (columns, lines, pie, scatter, waterfall…). There are more than 25 types. The chart floats over the grid: drag to move, pull the corner to resize, and the side editor changes the type, series and colors. It follows the data when it changes.

Gantt (task schedule with Start and End): in the panel, Series ▸ Schedule turns on the today line and colors each task by status (done, in progress, upcoming), worked out from today's date; the three colors are set there, and Points colors one bar by hand.

Sparklines: Insert → Sparklines (Line, Column or Win/Loss) draws a small chart inside the cell. Enter the data range and the location (a row or column of cells; each one gets one row or column of the data). With the cell selected, the Sparkline tab changes the type, highlights high, low, negative, first and last points, changes the style, uses the same axis for the group or clears it.
Images: Inserir → Imagem, paste (Ctrl+V) or drop the file on the grid.
• Review → New comment annotates the cell; hovering shows the balloon. Previous and Next go through comments; Show all comments keeps them all visible.
• Home → Clear → Clear comments removes the ones in the selection.

• Review → Protect Sheet (or Protect Workbook) blocks changes; in Home → Format you can lock or unlock cells first. Review → Allow Edit Ranges keeps ranges editable with the sheet protected, with an optional password (asked when you type in the range).
The Draw tab writes on top of the spreadsheet: pens and highlighter, Stroke eraser or Point eraser, and Lasso to select strokes. Esc goes back to normal selection.
• Ink to shape turns the stroke into a rectangle, ellipse or arrow.
• With a drawing tablet, the thickness follows the pen pressure (Settings → Spreadsheet). Without one, a fast stroke comes out thinner.
• Each stroke is one Ctrl+Z, and drawings are saved in .fshz and .xlsx.
Page Layout: Margins, Orientation, paper Size, Print area, Breaks, Scale to Fit (pages wide and tall, or a scale) and Print gridlines.
Preview shows the pages before printing. Insert → Header & footer adds text at the top and bottom of each page.
All of this is kept in the sheet and saved with the file (.fshz and .xlsx): opening an .xlsx brings the margins, paper, print area and header Excel saved.
• Find and replace: Ctrl+H.
• On the Data tab: Duplicates, Trim spaces, Split text (separator and type of each column, with preview), Statistics and Column profile (distribution, blanks, distinct values and outliers).

• In Split text, the preview shows every column (scroll sideways). Click a column name to pick it; Ctrl+click adds another and Shift+click selects the range. The type you choose applies to all selected columns.
• Data validation (ribbon, Data tab): drop-down list, number between limits, date, text — warning or rejecting on entry.

• FeatherQuery (Dados → FeatherQuery…): imports and transforms data — filter, group, merge tables, web sources — and keeps the steps so you can refresh later. In the query list, the clock turns on "Refresh when opening the file": the query is recalculated every time the file opens (file and Web sources use the saved copy). The ⋮ (or right-click) of a query renames it (queries that reference it follow the new name) and moves it to a folder: folders group queries in the panel and open or close with a click. Right-click a step to give it a name and a description (shown on mouse over), saved with the query. Get Data ▾ ▸ File ▸ Excel Web Query (.iqy) opens a Web query saved by Excel: the address becomes a Web source and the table chosen in the file is imported. Transform has Replace values/errors, Fill down/up, Format text (trim, UPPERCASE, Capitalize Each Word, prefix…), Transpose, Split by position and Extract from date; Home has Remove rows (top, bottom, blank) and Reverse rows; Add column has Custom column (a spreadsheet formula with [Column]: =[Price]*[Qty]) and Conditional column. Group by takes several aggregations at once, and Merge queries has fuzzy matching (similar names, ignoring accents and punctuation). Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y undo and redo steps. Duplicate query copies the open query as a connection; Reference query creates a new one that starts from its result (and recalculates it on refresh). Each command is one step. On a type change, what does not convert becomes #VALUE!, and a yellow bar counts them and offers to remove those rows or replace them with 0. From file also takes .fshz, .xlsm and .parquet; From folder joins every file in a folder into one table (the File column tells where each row came from; Re-read the folder picks up new ones). View ▸ Dependencies shows where each query reads from and writes to. An .xlsx or .fshz file with several sheets opens the Navigator: choose the sheet or table (Ctrl+T) to import, with a preview; title rows above the header are skipped. The query script lives in the Advanced editor (Home ▸ Query or View): line numbers, colors, a method list that writes the step at the cursor, and the error underlined on its line. The sheet chosen in the Navigator becomes the script's second line, fonte.planilha("Dados"); (or fonte.tabela("Sales");): change the name there and Apply re-reads the file with that sheet, if it has the same columns. Home ▸ Get data ▾ gathers every connection: File (Excel, FeatherSheet, Text/CSV, JSON, Parquet or a whole folder), Web, a table or sheet in this workbook, the selection, Enter data (in a dialog), another query as a reference and the recent sources. Filter takes conditions on several columns (all, AND, or any, OR, with contains, begins with, is blank…) or the list of values with check boxes, as in Excel. Extract text takes what comes before, after or between delimiters, the first or last characters or the length (Transform replaces the column; Add column creates another). Move (left, right, start, end) and Duplicate column are on the ribbon and on the column menu; renaming or moving several times in a row becomes a single step. Excel Power Query: paste the M (the text from Excel's Advanced Editor) into the Advanced editor and click Apply — the steps Excel writes from its buttons (filter, change type, group, merge, split, custom column…) become FeatherQuery steps, and anything without an equivalent stays as a "// M not converted:" comment for you to review. Opened an .xlsx with Power Query? Home ▸ Get data ▾ ▸ Power Query queries in this file lists the queries Excel saved in the file; the one you pick opens in the Advanced editor already converted. The Copy as Power Query button goes the other way: it puts the M for the steps on the clipboard, ready to paste into Excel.

Macros are JavaScript (Macros → Macro editor, or Alt+F11). Ctrl+Enter runs, and Ctrl+Z undoes the whole macro. When you type sheet. (or the start of a name), a list shows the methods with how to use them and an example: ↑/↓ choose, Tab or Enter write it, Esc closes. "Run on open" runs the macro every time the spreadsheet opens — that is how custom functions keep working.

Each spreadsheet keeps its own macros inside the .fshz file (like Excel's .xlsm): a new spreadsheet starts with none, and opening an .xlsm brings its VBA converted. To move macros between files, use Export and Import in the editor.
Inserir → Botão de macro creates a button on the grid that runs a macro when clicked. Drag to move; right-click to edit or delete.
Every function a macro can use is in the "Macros" section of this Help.

Opening an .xlsm converts its VBA macros to JavaScript. Before any macro from the file runs, the app asks "Enable macros?" — only accept if you trust the source. Saving as .xlsm (or as .fshz) keeps the original VBA project unchanged, with its forms and the link to each sheet, and Excel runs the macros as before; .xlsx carries no macros, as in Excel.

The converter understands VBA's text, number and date functions, the Format family (FormatNumber, FormatCurrency, FormatDateTime…), Choose, Switch, StrComp and the financial ones (Pmt, PV, FV, NPV, IRR, Rate…). Shell becomes app.shell, which shows the command and asks before running it. A ByRef parameter changed by the Sub or Function passes the new value back to the caller, as in Excel. CreateObject("WScript.Shell").Run also becomes app.shell, and Range.AutoFilter (with Criteria1, xlFilterValues, xlOr of two values and top 10), ShowAllData and AutoFilterMode = False use the sheet's AutoFilter. MsgBox has every button set (Abort/Retry/Ignore, Yes/No/Cancel…), icons and default button; Rnd and Randomize give the same sequence as Excel; CallByName with a fixed name, CCur with 4 decimals, Format's named formats (Scientific, Yes/No, Medium Time…) and StrConv width and kana also convert. Worksheet_SelectionChange becomes the On selecting cells event: it runs when the selection changes on the sheet (when dragging, on mouse release), with the address in valores.intervalo. Anything without an equivalent stays in the code as a "VBA não convertido" comment. Also converted: SpecialCells (the filter's visible cells, blanks, constants, formulas, the last used cell), which gives a multi-area range to copy, count, loop over or delete the rows of; AutoFilter with two conditions (xlAnd/xlOr); AdvancedFilter (copy and in place, with Unique); InputBox and Application.InputBox (Type 1, 2, 4 and 8), with a box to type in; the Mid(s, i, n) = x statement; Dictionary with CompareMode and Key; reading a shape's Left/Top/Width/Height. Numbers become text as in Excel, with the decimal separator of the app language and up to 15 digits.

Forms (VBA's UserForm): in the macro editor (Alt+F11), draw the window with text boxes, lists, options and buttons, and link each button to a macro. In a macro, sheet.showComponent("name") opens the form. Tab and Shift+Tab move through the typing fields in the TabIndex order that came from Excel (or the one in the control's "Tab order" property, in the editor; without it, the drawing order), and the form opens with the first field ready for typing.
A long macro runs in the background: the app shows it is running, with the elapsed time and a Stop button.

The native format is .fshz. Ctrl+S saves and Ctrl+Shift+S (Save as…) saves under another name as .fshz, .xlsx or .xlsm. An open .xlsx or .xlsm is saved back in the same format by Ctrl+S. Open also reads .csv, .tsv and .parquet.
Arquivo → Exportar writes the workbook as .xlsx or the current sheet as .csv.

A password-protected .xlsx (Excel or LibreOffice) opens: the app asks for the password, used only to decrypt the file on your machine. Review › Encrypt with password sets, changes or removes the password: the .xlsx is encrypted as in Excel (AES-256), and an opened file keeps its password when saved again. The .fshz does not keep a password: with a password set, Save suggests .xlsx and Ctrl+S on a .fshz asks where to save.
This help can become a file too: in the Help window (F1), Export as Markdown saves everything to a .md, in the app's language.

Autosave works ONLY for .fshz files that were already saved: it writes over them at the interval chosen in Settings. An opened .xlsx, .csv or .parquet file, or a new spreadsheet, is never written automatically — to use autosave, choose Save as… and pick .fshz.

Automatic recovery covers everything else: it keeps a copy of any changed spreadsheet (including .xlsx, .parquet and never-saved ones) in Documents/FeatherSheet/Temporarios/Recuperacao. If the computer shuts down, it shows up on the start screen to recover. It does not replace saving: the copy is removed when you save or discard. Very large workbooks (over 100 million cells) get no automatic copy, because each copy would freeze the window and double the memory: save them with Ctrl+S.
Everything runs on your machine: no account, no login, none of your content leaves it.
Settings ▸ Save new workbooks as .xlsx: Save as… suggests the Excel format.

☰ Menu ▸ Info ▸ Properties: the workbook's title, subject, author, manager, company, category, tags and comments, as in Excel. Saved in .fshz and .xlsx; created, last modified and last modified by are filled in automatically.

In Settings: light or dark theme, color scheme and accent, grid font and size, zoom, autosave, language (which also decides the formula separator) and keyboard shortcuts. In View › Zoom to Selection, the selected area fills the screen.
View → Monitor (or F12) shows memory, processor and the Console with what the app logged — useful to send along with a bug report.

Updates: on startup, FeatherSheet checks GitHub for a new version (at most once a day) and, if there is one, shows a card in the corner with What's new, Later and Update. Turn it off in Settings → About → Notify about new versions; the Check for updates button checks right away.
Settings ▸ Your details: name, initials and organization, saved as the files' author, "last modified by" and company, and used to sign comments (the same as in Getting started).

atalhosFixos.fimDosDados: Jump to the end of the data
atalhosFixos.executarMacro: Run the macro (in the Macros panel)

macros.introducao: Macros are JavaScript. The spreadsheet is the sheet object. Ctrl+Enter runs, and everything the macro does is undone at once with Ctrl+Z. Addresses use A1 notation ("B2", "A1:D10"); numeric rows and columns start at 1.

secoes.excel-navegacao: Finding data and moving between ranges

funcoes.cell: Like VBA: cell, cells and range without a sheet use the active sheet (where the macro runs). Another sheet only when written: sheets("Sales").cell("A1") or sheets(2).
funcoes.value: The computed value of the cell.
funcoes.formula: The text typed in the cell, starting with "=" when it is a formula.
funcoes.set: Writes a value or a formula into the cell. Returns `sheet`, so calls chain: `sheet.set("A1", 1).set("A2", 2)`.
funcoes.clear: Clears the content and the formatting of the cell or range (the VBA `Range.Clear`). To clear only one: `clearContents` and `clearFormats`.
funcoes.style: Formats the cell or range with an object. Returns `sheet`, for chaining. The keys are in "Formatting", below.
funcoes.range: A range, with the functions below. They can be chained.
funcoes.Range.formulas: Matrix with the typed text (formulas included).
funcoes.Range.set: A single value fills the whole range; a matrix is pasted from the corner.
funcoes.Range.forEach: Walks through the cells. Row and column start at 0, inside the range.
funcoes.Range.map: Writes into each cell what the function returns (undefined leaves it unchanged).
funcoes.Range.rows: How many rows and columns the range has.
funcoes.style-keys: Text: bold, italic, underline, strikethrough; text and fill color as "#rrggbb"; size and font.
funcoes.style-layout: align: "left" | "center" | "right"; vAlign: "top" | "middle" | "bottom"; wrap: wrap text; rotation: degrees from -90 to 90.
funcoes.style-number: format: "auto", "number", "integer", "currency", "accounting", "percent", "scientific", "date", "datetime", "time", "duration" or "text"; decimals: fixed decimal places.
funcoes.selection: The range selected in the grid.
funcoes.select: Selects a cell or range and scrolls to it. Returns `sheet`.
funcoes.lastRow: Number (starting at 1) of the last row and last column with data.
funcoes.address: The A1 address of a numeric row and column (starting at 1).
funcoes.sheets: The names of all sheets, in tab order.
funcoes.name: The name of the sheet where the macro started running.
funcoes.goToSheet: Goes to another sheet, like clicking its tab. Good for a macro button that navigates. The rest of the macro keeps writing to the sheet where it started.
funcoes.showComponent: Opens a component (an HTML and CSS screen built in the macro editor, Alt+F11) in a small window. Inside it, an element with data-macro="module" runs that module on click (fields with a name arrive in the variable valores) and data-fechar closes the window.
funcoes.defineFunction: Creates a function to use in cells (=TAX(D2)). Ranges arrive as a list. Check "Run on open" so it keeps working.
funcoes.log: Writes to the panel output box.
funcoes.status: Shows a short message in the status bar.
funcoes.get: The calculated value of the cell (for a range, the top-left one). The VBA `Range.Value`.
funcoes.setFormula: Writes a formula. On a range, relative references adjust cell by cell, like Excel. Returns `sheet` for chaining.
funcoes.setFormulaR1C1: Writes a formula in R1C1 notation (`R[0]C[-2]` is relative, `R3C4` is absolute).
funcoes.getText: The text exactly as it appears on screen, with the format applied (`Range.Text`).
funcoes.setNumberFormat: Applies an Excel number mask: `"#,##0.00"`, `"0%"`, `"dd/mm/yyyy"`, `"R$ #,##0.00"`, `"@"`. It also accepts a custom code, such as `"dd"`, `"mmmm/yyyy"` or `"0 \"kWh\""`. A code the app does not understand raises an error.
funcoes.clearContents: Clears only values and formulas; the formatting stays (`ClearContents`).
funcoes.clearFormats: Clears only the formatting; the values stay (`ClearFormats`).
funcoes.copy: Copies and pastes. `paste`: `"all"` (default), `"values"`, `"formulas"` or `"formats"`. Formulas adjust to the new place. `to` is the top-left corner of the destination.
funcoes.move: Moves content and formatting elsewhere. Formulas that referred to the source follow (`Range.Cut`).
funcoes.find: The address of the first cell (topmost, leftmost) that has the text, or `null`. `range` narrows the search; `inFormulas` searches what was typed.
funcoes.replace: Replaces text inside the range; returns how many cells changed.
funcoes.getAddress: The A1 address of a range.
funcoes.autoFill: Fills a series, like dragging the handle: 1, 2, 3…, dates, numbered text, formulas. Returns how many cells it filled.
funcoes.setFontSize: Font size in **pixels** (the sheet default is 13).
funcoes.setUnderline: Underline: `"single"`/`true` on, `"none"`/`false` off. Double becomes single.
funcoes.setFontColor: Text color: `"#RRGGBB"` or the VBA number (`app.rgb(r, g, b)`).
funcoes.setWrapText: Wraps the text onto several lines inside the cell.
funcoes.setHyperlink: Puts a link on the cell; `text` (optional) is what it shows.
funcoes.setBorder: Borders, merging with the existing ones: `top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`, `insideH`, `insideV`, `all`, `none` and `color`. Only a thin solid line exists; a different `style` or `width` raises an error.
funcoes.setOutline: The outer outline of the range in one call (`BorderAround`).
funcoes.autoFitColumns: Fits the column width to the content, like double-clicking the border (`"A:F"`, `"B"`).
funcoes.autoFitColumn: Fits the column width to its content. Only on the sheet on screen.
funcoes.hideRow: Hides the row (or shows it again with `false`).
funcoes.hideColumn: Hides the column (or shows it again with `false`).
funcoes.insertRow: Inserts rows before the row, pushing the rest down. Only on the sheet on screen; goes into the structure Ctrl+Z.
funcoes.insertColumn: Inserts columns before the column, pushing the rest right. Only on the sheet on screen.
funcoes.deleteRow: Deletes rows. Only on the sheet on screen.
funcoes.deleteColumn: Deletes columns. Only on the sheet on screen.
funcoes.deleteCells: Deletes the cells and pulls the cells below ("up") or to the right ("left") into place, like Excel's Delete cells….
funcoes.insertCells: Inserts empty cells and pushes the selection down ("down") or right ("right").
funcoes.rowCount: How many rows the range has.
funcoes.columnCount: How many columns the range has.
funcoes.cell: The cell at row and column (the first is 1), as a range.
funcoes.getLastRow: Number of the last row with data in the column; 0 if the column is empty. The `Cells(Rows.Count, 1).End(xlUp).Row`.
funcoes.getLastColumn: Number of the last column with data in the row; 0 if the row is empty.
funcoes.getDataRange: The smallest rectangle containing everything used (`UsedRange`), or `null` if the sheet is empty.
funcoes.getRegion: The contiguous block of data around the cell (`CurrentRegion`, Ctrl+Shift+*).
funcoes.offset: Shifts the range by rows and columns (negative goes up/left).
funcoes.resize: A range of `rows` × `cols` from the top-left cell.
funcoes.columnOf: Column `n` (the first is 1) inside the range.
funcoes.rowOf: Row `n` (the first is 1) inside the range.
funcoes.merge: Merges the cells; only the top-left content stays.
funcoes.unmerge: Undoes the merges the range touches.
funcoes.isMerged: Is the cell part of a merged region?
funcoes.specialCells: The addresses of the cells in the range of a kind: `"blanks"`, `"formulas"`, `"constants"`, `"errors"` or `"visible"` (those not in a hidden row or column; an AutoFilter requested earlier in the same macro counts too).
funcoes.specialAreas: The same cells as `specialCells`, joined into areas: `"A1:C2,A4:C4"` (empty when there are none; VBA's `SpecialCells`). A multi-area range works in the API: writing, clearing and formatting touch every area; `copy` pastes the areas together, without the gaps (the visible rows of a filter, one under the other); `value` and `rows` read the first area, as in Excel; sort, move and merge refuse.
funcoes.activeCell: The focused cell: the top-left corner of the selection.
funcoes.intersect: The intersection of two ranges, or `null` if they do not touch.
funcoes.sort: Sorts by one or more columns (`order`: `"asc"` or `"desc"`). `header: true` keeps the first row in place.
funcoes.removeDuplicates: Removes duplicate rows (by the given columns, or all); returns how many were removed.
funcoes.setDataValidation: Data validation: `{ type: "list", values }` or `source: "A1:A5"`; `"number"` (`operator` between/greaterThan/lessThan/equal, `min`, `max`, `value`); `"date"`; `"text"`; `"checkbox"`. `errorMessage` and `mode: "warn"` (the default is to reject).
funcoes.clearDataValidation: Removes the validation from the range.
funcoes.addConditionalFormat: Conditional formatting: `{ type: "cellValue", operator, value, value2, fill, color, bold, italic }` or `{ type: "formula", formula, fill }`. Operators of the panel: greaterThan, between, textContains, duplicate, aboveAverage…
funcoes.addColorScale: A color scale from the smallest to the largest value.
funcoes.clearConditionalFormats: Removes the conditional formatting rules that touch the range.
funcoes.wb.sheet: The API (`sheet`) of another sheet, by name or position (the first is 1). Inserting/deleting rows and columns only works on the sheet on screen.
funcoes.wb.addSheet: Creates a new sheet and returns its API.
funcoes.wb.deleteSheet: Removes the sheet (the workbook needs at least one).
funcoes.wb.copySheet: Duplicates the sheet and returns the copy's API.
funcoes.wb.moveSheet: Moves the sheet to the position (the first is 1).
funcoes.wb.setSheetVisible: Shows or hides the sheet (the workbook needs one visible).
funcoes.wb.activate: Brings the sheet to the front.
funcoes.wb.freezePanes: Freezes the top rows and left columns.
funcoes.wb.addName: Names a range (on the active sheet, or written as `"Plan1!A1:A10"`).
funcoes.wb.sheetCount: How many sheets the workbook has (a property, no parentheses).
funcoes.wb.addSheet: Creates a sheet (optional name: Planilha4…) before or after another (sheet or name); with no position, before the active one. The new sheet becomes active and is returned.
funcoes.wb.deleteSheet: Deletes the sheet (object or name). The workbook always keeps at least one visible sheet; if the macro fails, the sheet comes back.
funcoes.wb.renameSheet: Renames the sheet (object or name); formulas that refer to it follow. Rejects an empty name, one with !, or a repeated one.
funcoes.wb.name: The name of the open document (a property, no parentheses).
funcoes.sheet.exportPdf: Exports this sheet to PDF, using the print area. The path is relative to the open file's folder (`\` becomes `/`). Returns `sheet`.
funcoes.sheet.saveAs: Saves only this sheet to a new file, `.xlsx` or `.fshz` (by extension). The path is relative to the open file's folder (`\` becomes `/`). Returns `sheet`.
funcoes.sheet.protect: Protects the sheet, like Format › Protect sheet (VBA's Protect). Optional password; permissions use the .xlsx names (formatCells, formatColumns, formatRows, insertColumns, insertRows, insertHyperlinks, deleteColumns, deleteRows, sort, autoFilter, pivotTables, objects, scenarios). Applied when the macro finishes successfully.
funcoes.sheet.unprotect: Removes the sheet protection (VBA's Unprotect). With a wrong password the sheet stays protected and a message is shown. Applied when the macro finishes successfully; the macro itself can already write to the protected sheet.
funcoes.sheet.showGridlines: Shows or hides this sheet's gridlines (VBA's ActiveWindow.DisplayGridlines).
funcoes.sheet.autoFilter: Turns on the AutoFilter on the range and, with the column (1 = first of the range), filters by it: text as in COUNTIF (">100", "SP", "<>"), a list of values (["SP", "RJ"]) or { op: "top10", n: 10 }; without criteria, clears the column. Rows hide when the macro finishes, and Ctrl+Z undoes it (VBA's AutoFilter). Two conditions: { op: "e", val: [">=10", "<=20"] } (AND; op: "ou" for OR). The macro itself already sees the filtered rows through specialCells(…, "visible").
funcoes.sheet.showAllData: showAllData() removes the criteria and keeps the filter arrows; autoFilterOff() removes the sheet's AutoFilter (VBA's ShowAllData and AutoFilterMode = False).
funcoes.sheet.advancedFilter: Excel's Advanced Filter: the list (the first row holds the headers) and the criteria range, with the same headers; each criteria row is an alternative (OR) and everything in it must hold (AND). The criterion is COUNTIF's (">100", "<>x", "a*"); text without an operator matches what begins with it, and "=SP" only the equal one. With { copyTo: "F4" } it copies the header and the matching rows there (sheet: "Sheet" for another sheet); without copyTo it hides the rows that do not match, and showAllData() shows them again. unique: true drops repeats (VBA's AdvancedFilter).
funcoes.sheet.pastePicture: Pastes the look of a range as a picture (VBA's CopyPicture): the picture sits over the grid with its corner on the cell, as the screen shows it (borders, colors, number formats, gridlines if they are on). { sheet: "Sheet" } takes the picture from another sheet. The returned object accepts .width and .height (in points; setting only one keeps the proportion). It is part of the macro's Ctrl+Z.
funcoes.sheet.shape: The shape or text box by the name it had in Excel ("TextBox 1"): `text` reads and changes the text, `font({…})` changes bold, italic, size and color ("#RRGGBB" or app.rgb) and `font()` reads it; `exists` tells whether the sheet has the shape. It is VBA's Shapes("…").TextFrame2.TextRange. `visible` hides or shows the shape, `onAction` changes the macro a click runs, and `left`, `top`, `width`, `height` (in points, as in VBA) or `move({…})` change position and size when the macro finishes. Reading `left`, `top`, `width` and `height` gives the current position in points (or the one the macro already asked for).
funcoes.wb.saveSheetsAs: Saves a new workbook with only the given sheets (list of names or numbers), as `.xlsx` or `.fshz`. The path is relative to the open file's folder (`\` becomes `/`).
funcoes.app.batch: Runs the block. The macro already runs in a single transaction (one Ctrl+Z undoes it all); it exists so code converted from VBA (`ScreenUpdating`) stays the same.
funcoes.app.shell: Runs a system program or command (VBA's Shell). It only runs after the macro finishes successfully and the user sees the command and clicks Run; if the code holds a binary stored as text (Base64, byte list, certutil…), it warns in red; this is not an antivirus. Returns 0.
funcoes.app.choose: Asks with up to 3 buttons and returns the index of the chosen one. Buttons are VBA MsgBox codes (1 OK, 2 Cancel, 3 Abort, 4 Retry, 5 Ignore, 6 Yes, 7 No); the icon is 16 critical, 32 question, 48 warning or 64 information; the default is the index of the Enter button. As with confirm, the macro runs again after the answer.
funcoes.prompt: The text the person types, or null when they cancel (VBA's InputBox). The second text comes filled in the field. As with confirm, the macro runs again after the answer.
funcoes.app.openUrl: Opens a web link in the browser (VBA's ShellExecute "open") after the macro finishes successfully. Only http, https, mailto and www., like a cell hyperlink; a file or program is not opened and a message is shown. Returns true.
funcoes.app.setEventsEnabled: Turns the event macros (on open, on activate, on change, on select) on or off. Turns back on by itself when the macro ends.
funcoes.app.rgb: The VBA `RGB(r, g, b)`: the color as a number (BGR order). The color functions accept the number or `"#RRGGBB"`.
funcoes.app.isError: Is the value a spreadsheet error (`#N/A`, `#DIV/0!`…)?
funcoes.app.error: Creates a spreadsheet error to write into a cell.
funcoes.app.fn.sum: Sum of the numbers; text and empty cells are ignored. Accepts a list or matrix (`range.values()`).
funcoes.app.fn.average: Average of the numbers; `#DIV/0!` if there are none.
funcoes.app.fn.countIf: Counts the values meeting the Excel criterion: `">5"`, `"<>x"`, case-insensitive text, `*` and `?` wildcards.
funcoes.app.fn.sumIf: Conditional sum: sums `sumValues` (or the values themselves) where `values` meets the criterion.
funcoes.app.fn.vlookup: Vertical lookup: finds the key in the 1st column and returns column `col` (the first is 1) of the same row. `#N/A` if not found. Exact match by default (`exact = false` accepts the largest value that does not exceed it).
funcoes.app.fn.hlookup: Horizontal lookup: like `vlookup`, searching the 1st row.
funcoes.app.fn.match: The position (the first is 1) of the value in the list: `0` exact, `1` the largest not exceeding (ascending), `-1` the smallest not below (descending). `#N/A` if not found.
funcoes.app.fn.index: The value at the position: `index(list, n)` or `index(matrix, row, col)` (the first is 1).
